help.tips[0].examples[0].en: We're saving in order to travel in the summer.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: I set three alarms in order to get up early tomorrow.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: A purpose with the same subject is um … zu; damit needs its own subject, and für cannot introduce a zu-infinitive.
help.tips[0].en.text: Ich lerne Deutsch, um hier zu arbeiten. Er ging früh los, um den Zug zu erreichen. Wozu? → um … zu. The zu-infinitive is last; a separable verb swallows the zu: um früh aufzustehen.
help.tips[0].en.title: um … zu = purpose (same subject)
help.tips[0].en.trap: English 'to' alone gives a purpose ('I'm learning German to work here'). German needs the um: 'Ich lerne Deutsch, zu arbeiten' is wrong.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: He left the house without saying goodbye.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: She signed the contract without reading it through.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: ohne opens the clause and zu + infinitive comes right at the end.
help.tips[1].en.text: Sie ging weg, ohne etwas zu sagen. Er kaufte das Auto, ohne die Preise zu vergleichen. Wie? → ohne … zu.
help.tips[1].en.title: ohne … zu = without -ing
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Instead of working, he sat in the café all day.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: Instead of taking the bus, she walked.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: statt needs zu + infinitive, and when the statt-clause comes first, the main verb follows straight after the comma.
help.tips[2].en.text: Er sah fern, statt zu lernen. Wir gingen zu Fuß, anstatt mit dem Bus zu fahren. Both statt and anstatt are correct.
help.tips[2].en.title: (an)statt … zu = instead of -ing
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: He left without saying hello. — He left without us noticing.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: She cooked instead of watching TV. — She cooked instead of us going out to eat.
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: The subjects differ (ich speaks, alle understand), so you need damit with its own subject, not an infinitive clause.
help.tips[3].en.text: Ich lerne, um zu arbeiten (I learn, I work). Ich lerne, damit meine Kinder stolz sind (I learn, they are proud). ohne zu / ohne dass, statt zu / statt dass follow the same split.
help.tips[3].en.title: Same subject? Infinitive. Different? damit / dass.
help.context.en: I came to Germany in order to study here. At first I went to every lecture without understanding a word. Instead of giving up, I did a language course to learn faster. Today I talk to everyone without thinking twice – and sometimes, instead of studying, I just go into town to hear German.
help.mistakes[0].whyEn: Purpose needs um, and zu + verb goes last.
help.mistakes[2].whyEn: zu goes inside a separable verb.
help.hookEn: Say why, how and instead of what in one smooth step: um hier zu arbeiten, ohne etwas zu sagen, statt zu lernen.
help.introEn: Three infinitive clauses that answer why, how and instead-of-what: um … zu (in order to), ohne … zu (without -ing), (an)statt … zu (instead of -ing). Ich lerne Deutsch, um in Berlin zu arbeiten. Sie ging weg, ohne etwas zu sagen. Er sah fern, statt zu lernen. All three take the zu-infinitive at the end, a comma before, and — the condition that decides whether you can use them — the same subject in both halves: the person who learns is the person who will work. When the subjects differ, um … zu becomes damit and ohne … zu becomes ohne dass (next quiz). um … zu is the most useful of the three: it is how you give a purpose in one smooth step — why you are here, why you called, why you are learning. In the quiz you place both parts yourself: um, ohne or (an)statt at the start of the clause, and zu + infinitive at the end — with the zu inside a separable verb (aufzustehen, durchzulesen).
help.rememberEn[0]: um … zu (why), ohne … zu (without), statt … zu (instead of) — zu-infinitive last, comma before.
help.rememberEn[1]: Only with the same subject in both halves.
sentences[0].whyEn: Purpose: um … zu arbeiten — um opens, zu + infinitive closes.
sentences[2].whyEn: The missing thing: ohne … zu sagen — 'without saying a word'.
sentences[4].whyEn: The alternative he did NOT pick: (an)statt … zu lernen.
sentences[8].whyEn: ohne … zu verabschieden — the sich stays before the zu.
sentences[9].whyEn: ohne … zu vergleichen — what he should have done.
sentences[10].whyEn: (An)statt … zu fahren — the alternative not taken.
sentences[11].whyEn: Purpose with a separable verb: the zu crawls inside — um … aufZUstehen.
sentences[14].whyEn: ohne … durchzulesen — separable, zu in the middle.
sentences[15].whyEn: um … zu erholen — with the reflexive uns before it.
sentences[16].whyEn: ohne … nachzudenken — separable: nach + zu + denken.
